title: Harden Tauri Python runtime provenance
summary: Bind productized Tauri backend startup to the bundled, release-manifest-verified Python runtime and an isolated release-owned import path.
reason: Partially remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W09-003. Release startup currently accepts ambient python.exe and inherited PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME state, allowing non-release code to execute before backend contract validation.
behavior_before: All build profiles try bundled candidates and then unconditionally accept the literal python command. Backend launch prepends release src to inherited PYTHONPATH and does not isolate user-site or Python-home state.
behavior_after: Release builds require apps/desktop/runtime/Python/python.exe and exactly matching path, byte-count, and SHA-256 evidence in the bounded root mediapipeline_release_manifest.v1. Debug builds alone retain explicit ambient fallback. Backend launch uses Python -I with a JSON-encoded release src bootstrap, removes inherited PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME/PYTHONUSERBASE/PYTHONSTARTUP, and disables user-site/safe-path fallbacks.
tests_added: A Rust integration test runs the real bundled Python with -I and the release-src-only bootstrap, proving local_api_main imports successfully without PYTHONPATH.
Rust fixtures prove a valid release-manifest path/size/hash resolves the exact bundled interpreter and debug mode alone retains ambient fallback.
Rust fixtures prove release mode rejects missing bundled Python, missing manifest evidence, and a SHA-256 mismatch without falling back to PATH.
The Python Tauri scaffold asserts the isolated-launch environment, manifest schema/path contract, debug-only mode switch, and direct SHA-256 dependency.

rollback_plan: Revert the Tauri runtime resolver, isolated Python bootstrap, sha2 dependency/lock entry, Rust/static tests, lifecycle documentation, and generated context together. Do not restore ambient release fallback independently.
